params.name: Drake
params.note: A very large luxury compound coaxial shaped like a mandarin drake. The pilot sits in the eye. A round head on a neck with a red bill, a green forehead and a white crescent, a plump violet breast on a boat hull that lands on water, white and black shoulder bars, a mane of a crest, orange sail fins, and paddle feet that fold away. Two stacked contra-rotating rotors and a ducted pusher, so no tail rotor.

cabin.note: The cockpit is the inside of the head and the windows are the eyes; the pilot sits on the centreline under the centre screen, the eyes either side. About 16 m from the bill to the fan. Read by client/shared/interior-drake.js.
cabin.head: head

parts.name: fuselage
parts.note: The neck, the breast, the back and the tail. The head is its own part, on top of the neck.

parts.name: head
parts.note: A round head on the neck: green forehead and crown, orange face, and the white crescent running back from the eye, which is the cockpit.

parts.name: bill
parts.note: A duck bill: deep at the root, flat and slightly waisted along its length, flaring to a broad rounded spatula, all one orange-red. The radar lives in here, and the QUACK comes out of it.

parts.name: crest
parts.note: The teardrop: fat over the back of the head, trailing to a point down the nape. Green over, violet under, a white line between, emerald to blue front to back.

parts.name: eye frame
parts.note: The white surround the crescent grows out of.

parts.name: eye window
parts.note: The cockpit: the pilot sits in the eye, painted in through the drakeeye canopy art.

parts.name: ruff
parts.note: The orange cheek ruff as separate quills standing off the head and lying back along the neck, so the silhouette breaks up. Alternate tones so neighbours separate. Rooted below and behind the eye window, clear of the cockpit.

parts.name: armour plate
parts.note: The brown armoured flank plate: a rounded shell standing just proud of the skin, with a raised lip round its edge and panel seams, laid on the fuselage facets so it cannot float off or sink in.

parts.name: spray rail
parts.note: The belly is a boat hull: with the feet folded up it sits on the water.

parts.name: sail
parts.note: The orange sail feather as a cupped fan shell behind the mast: it leans out, bulges, and has a thickness, with alternating vanes so it reads as feathers rather than a board.

parts.name: wing pivot
parts.note: The swing-wing pivot box the wing turns on.

parts.name: wings
parts.note: Swing wings. Folded (wings 0) they lie back along the flanks the way a duck's do; spread (wings 1) they turn it into a plane.

parts.name: wing fold
parts.note: A bird folds a wing in three motions: it rolls down against the flank (the innermost hinge), swings back along the body, and sits outboard of it, so the folded wing covers the upper flank like a cloak with the primaries crossing the rump.

parts.name: wing brake
parts.note: The lean (drake-water.js): with the wings out, each wing pitches up about its root until it stands across the airflow, the way a duck brakes onto water. Nothing at brake 0.

parts.name: wing
parts.note: The swing wing, built as a bird wing: marginal and greater coverts over a white leading edge, the speculum with white tips, tertials at the root, and slotted primaries fanned at the hand. Folded (wings 0) it lies back along the flank; spread (wings 1) it spans about 0.95 a side, and folded it ends just ahead of the tail fan.

parts.name: pylon
parts.note: The faired pylon the mast rises out of, behind the head. In plane mode the rotor head goes down inside it.

parts.name: pylon seal
parts.note: The collar the rotor head telescopes through: a thin brass ring at the top of the pylon.

parts.name: pylon neck
parts.note: Telescopes down into the pylon as the rotor tucks.

parts.name: rotor head
parts.note: Mast and both hubs: slides down by TUCK in plane mode, the same number as the rotors fold.tuck.

parts.name: lower rotor disc
parts.note: Schematic only: the blades are drawn from rotors[0].

parts.name: upper rotor disc
parts.note: Schematic only: rotors[1], turning the other way.

parts.name: tail
parts.note: In BOAT mode the boom swings down at its root and puts the ducted pusher under the water; the hull stays level.

parts.name: fin
parts.note: The tail fin, on the boom: it swings down with it in BOAT mode.

parts.name: pusher fan
parts.note: Counter-turned against the boom as it drops, so the fan still pushes straight aft under the water.

parts.name: fan ring
parts.note: The ringed fan at the end of the boom: the pusher that drives it as a plane.

parts.name: blade crutch
parts.note: Rises out of the boom to take the folded blade tips, and sinks back into it in heli mode.

parts.name: minigun
parts.note: One a side under the breast: six barrels in a housing on a stub. Toed in about 4.1° so the two guns converge 6 ahead of the nose.

parts.name: rear ramp
parts.note: The underside of the tail cone, hinged at the cabin floor. The RAMP button drops it to the ground.

parts.name: ramp jack
parts.note: The pair of rams that lower it; the upper ends are in the cabin.

parts.name: ramp extension
parts.note: Stowed inside the ramp; turns with it and then telescopes out of its end to the ground.

parts.name: saloon
parts.note: Six seats in three rows, seen through the open ramp; drawn only while it is open.

parts.name: bay
parts.note: The dark bay the feet fold into, laid on the belly facets themselves so it can never stand off or sink into the hull.

parts.name: inner door
parts.note: The keel-side leaf: lifts straight up into the hull like a plug door. It cannot hinge on the keel, because the keel is curved, and a leaf swung about a straight line off a curved one sweeps its ends across the centreline into its twin.

parts.name: outer door
parts.note: The flank-side leaf. It slides up inside the hull like the inner leaf rather than swinging out: swung out it hung exactly where the minigun was later mounted, and read as a pale square over the gun.

parts.name: foot
parts.note: Retracts like a main gear: the toes curl shut first, then the whole leg swings up and inboard about its hip into the bay, over the last two-thirds of the gear channel after the door has opened.

parts.name: oleo cylinder
parts.note: The retraction jack: rides up into the bay with the leg.

parts.name: toe fold
parts.note: The toes curl up round the ankle before the leg moves, so the foot goes into the bay folded rather than spread.

parts.name: web
parts.note: Duck feet are webbed: a membrane between the three forward toes, sagging a little below them.

parts.name: ankle housing
parts.note: A cast housing round the ankle joint: the leg drops into it and the foot pivots out of it.

parts.name: snapped leg
parts.note: What is left when the feet snap off on the water.
